title: "Where malaria, open defecation, and child anemia coincide"
subtitle: "A geospatial typology of DHS survey clusters in sub-Saharan Africa"

```{python}
from IPython.display import HTML
from _common import summary, csv
s = summary()
p = csv("kmeans_profiles.csv").set_index("profile_name")
sc = csv("model_scores.csv").set_index("model")
hs = csv("dbscan_summary.csv")
top = p.loc["All three high"]
HTML(f"""
<div class="stat-row">
 <div class="stat"><div class="num">{s['children']:,}</div><div class="lbl">children aged 6–59 months tested for anemia</div></div>
 <div class="stat"><div class="num">{s['clusters']:,}</div><div class="lbl">survey clusters (villages / neighbourhoods)</div></div>
 <div class="stat"><div class="num">{s['countries']}</div><div class="lbl">countries, {s['surveys']} DHS surveys, {s['year_min']}–{s['year_max']}</div></div>
 <div class="stat"><div class="num">{s['anemia_pct']:.0f}%</div><div class="lbl">of children anemic in the average cluster</div></div>
</div>""")
```

**Anemia** affects most young children in sub-Saharan Africa, and it slows growth and learning. Two well-known causes are **malaria**, which destroys red blood cells, and poor **sanitation**: when households have no toilet, worm infections and gut inflammation follow. This project asks where these problems **pile up in the same places**, whether places fall into a few recognisable **profiles**, and how well open defecation, malaria, rainfall, and household conditions can **predict** anemia.

## Three things this project found

```{python}
HTML(f"""
<div class="finding"><b>1. One in ten clusters has all three problems at once.</b> In the "all three high" profile,
{top.anemia_pct:.0f}% of children are anemic, {top.od_pct:.0f}% of households have no toilet, and malaria prevalence is {top.pfpr:.0f}%.
These clusters are poorer and more rural than the rest.</div>
<div class="finding"><b>2. They are concentrated in one belt.</b> DBSCAN finds {len(hs)} hotspots. The largest
({hs.n_clusters.iloc[0]:,} clusters) stretches across {hs.countries.iloc[0]}.</div>
<div class="finding"><b>3. Malaria and neighbourhood matter most for predicting anemia.</b> A random forest explains
{sc.loc['Random forest','test_r2']*100:.0f}% of the variation in cluster anemia, against {sc.loc['Linear regression','test_r2']*100:.0f}% for a linear model.
Anemia in nearby clusters and malaria are the strongest predictors. Open defecation adds little once those are known.</div>
""")
```

## The "all three high" belt at a glance

Each hexagon is coloured by the **share of its survey clusters in the "all three high" profile**. Hover for details.

```{python}
import altair as alt
from _common import hexes, regions
hx = hexes()
base = alt.Chart(regions(0.05)).mark_geoshape(fill="#f4f4f4", stroke="#c4c4c4", strokeWidth=0.4)
h = alt.Chart(hx).mark_geoshape(stroke="white", strokeWidth=0.15).encode(
    color=alt.Color("profile1_pct:Q", title="% of clusters 'all three high'",
                    scale=alt.Scale(scheme="reds", domain=[0, 100]),
                    legend=alt.Legend(orient="left", gradientLength=220)),
    tooltip=[alt.Tooltip("country:N"), alt.Tooltip("profile1_pct:Q", title="% all three high", format=".0f"),
             alt.Tooltip("anemia_pct:Q", title="Anemia %", format=".0f"),
             alt.Tooltip("od_pct:Q", title="No toilet %", format=".0f"),
             alt.Tooltip("pfpr:Q", title="Malaria %", format=".0f"),
             alt.Tooltip("n_clusters:Q", title="DHS clusters")])
(base + h).project("equalEarth").properties(width=820, height=640).configure_view(stroke=None)
```
